# Independent audit: strict open-cover and independent-normal profiles



Source: `candidate eaf48fc18423f63a`.

**Result: PASS.** I read the whole source and its exact theorem dependency
`candidate 55fd8fec61360536`. The latter has the
independent audit explicitly cited by the source; this note checks the new
strictness deductions, not a new equality classification for densities.

## 1. Strict open-cover lemma

For alpha>0, if the nominal retained mass M-R is nonpositive, the claimed
profile is already strict. Otherwise distal truncation leaves a closed
convex set L with positive density mass and every original cap has
restricted mass at most alpha. The hereditary theorem gives an attained
depth point in U intersect int L: replacing the restricted positive
support by this open intersection changes only a Lebesgue-null boundary.

The finite open-cover hypothesis gives an original cap whose interior
contains that point. A small ball lies simultaneously in U, int L and
the cap interior. The inverse-power potential is finite positive and
continuous on U; on a smaller closed ball it is bounded above and
bounded away from zero. In particular the density has a strictly
positive lower bound there. Translating the selected cap to the point
loses at least the open half of this ball outside the translated cap,
so the mass loss is strictly positive. Its translated cap still has
the hereditary lower mass gamma times the retained mass. The resulting
strict inequality has the stated sign and coefficient.

This verifies strictness even with full or empty original cap traces.
The alpha>0 restriction is essential and was not dropped. Every
hyperplane has zero density mass, so closed boundaries introduce no
untracked positive mass. No bounded-support hypothesis is required;
the positive slab is located in one fixed local interior ball.

## 2. Independent-normal projective case

For an inclusion-minimal j-cap cover with j independent original
normals, the affine margin image is full-dimensional. Its separation
from the open negative orthant gives a nonzero nonnegative coefficient
vector lambda. A zero coefficient would leave a proper subcover, so
all entries are strictly positive. Independence makes their weighted
margin sum t nonconstant. It is positive on the original body's
interior and its zero set is volume-null.

The audited projective marginal construction therefore applies with
target dimension j-1 and inverse-power exponent j. After division by
t, the exact weighted margin sum is 1. At least one margin is strictly
positive at every projective point, giving precisely the open-cover
hypothesis, not only an almost-everywhere cover.

No projected margin can be constant: that would make the corresponding
original affine margin proportional to t, and independence of the
original normals would force all other positive entries of lambda to
vanish. This is impossible for j>=2. Thus the projected traces are
actual halfspaces as required by the strict-cover lemma. All original
cap masses and total volume are preserved by the projective marginal.
Applying Section 1 proves strictness with gamma_(j-1).

## 3. Nonminimal covers and endpoint parameters

For a strictly smaller minimal subcover, the ordinary effective-count
profile uses gamma_(j'-1), with gamma_0=1 for a one-cap cover. Since
gamma_r strictly decreases with r, replacing this denominator by
gamma_(j-1) increases the profile strictly whenever alpha>0. All
restored cap summands are nonnegative. This proves the nonminimal
case without requiring any of the omitted cap masses to be positive.

The claimed overlap form is obtained only when a=min A_i>0, at which
point every positive-part term is A_i-a; its rearrangement is correct.
The result is strict for each fixed independent-normal configuration,
but supplies no uniform gap as the normals approach dependence. The
source explicitly preserves that distinction and makes no arithmetic
or mixed-fiber summation claim.
